source: Re-verified 2026-09-07 (core/verify_gem_choices.py-equivalent methodology, active chase-bonus set forced empty first so an ALREADY-listed item can be genuinely re-checked, not compared against itself - see revalidate_chase_bonus.py in NOTES.md). Real, necessary consequence of the 2026-09-06 phase-legal-gem fix: gem_optimizer._all_gems() now also excludes unique/requiredProfession-gated gems, so the off-color "best gem of this color" representative used to build a chase-bonus loadout got weaker for several colors (e.g. RED: "Crimson Sun" 33131, unique+Jewelcrafting-only, excluded -> "Bright Crimson Spinel" 32197). Any item whose real win margin depended on that now-illegal substitute flips to a real, resolved loss; item_ids below are the real, re-confirmed 30k-iteration result. 29095 (Pauldrons of Malorne) added 2026-09-07 - the shoulder/gem-optimizer investigation below: real +2.15 DPS win with hybrid gems [24056, 24059] (matching wowsims' own real picks exactly), verified with the meta requirement held valid on both sides and a real-sim-tested (not crude-score-only) gem shortlist. The new top-level 'gems' map is required for this one: chase_bonus_gems_for_item()'s own crude-score fallback (used when no override exists) picks a DIFFERENT, real-sim-confirmed-worse gem (Great Dawnstone, pure Yellow) for the second socket instead of the actually-verified winner (Potent Noble Topaz, Orange) - see gem_optimizer.py's own module notes on why crude score alone isn't trusted for this. Every other, older entry in item_ids has no override here and still falls back to crude-score-derived gems, matching their own original, real verification (which didn't hit this same specific tie-break trap).
